note: Adapted from Hill's (1942) species-level description, the original in English; the original uses the old combination Eutermes dixoni (now placed in Nasutitermes). Measurement figures are retained verbatim; the queen measurements follow the alate section in the original and are listed separately here under 'Other'.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The original (Hill 1942) follows the combination Eutermes dixoni Hill, 1932. The alate is small and dark brown, intermediate in size between E. fumigatus and E. exitiosus; the soldier is small, with the head pale yellow and the nasus rusty; the worker is yellow above on the head, becoming pale brown posteriorly.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: A small dark brown species, intermediate in size between E. fumigatus and E. exitiosus (the latter two have roughly the same distribution as this species). Head, antennae, pronotum and abdominal tergites darkest, the postclypeus pale yellow tinged with brown, the wings dark brown, usually with a distinct clear area between the media and the cubitus in the basal half of the wing, the veins very dark. Postclypeus length less than half its width. Mandibular teeth 1 and 2 about equal in size. Fontanelle often indistinct. Antennae 15-segmented; segment 3 smallest; segments 4 and 6 larger than segment 5 (Fig. 106). Measurements: length with wings 14.00—15.50; length without wings 5.50—6.50; head length (to anterior margin of clypeus) 1.40—1.45; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.80—0.88; head width 1.14—1.22; maximum diameter of compound eye 0.29—0.36; ocellus length 0.11—0.12; pronotum length 0.51—0.59; pronotum width 0.90—1.00; forewing length 11.50—12.00; forewing width 3.30—3.75.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Small, the head pale yellow, the nasus rusty, becoming orange-yellow towards the base. Head fawn yellow, palest posteriorly, thickly covered with brown above and on the sides, sparsely hairy, variable in size, the posterior half hemispherical (Fig. 107); nasus varying in length, usually moderately stout at the base, sometimes very stout, about one third of the total head length, the head in side view (Fig. 108) either nearly straight or distinctly concave slightly behind the middle. Antennae usually 13-segmented, rarely 12 or 14; segment 4 usually shortest, segment 2 sometimes shortest. Measurements: total length 3.50—4.00; head length (to apex of nasus) 1.55—1.83; head width 0.95—1.15; pronotum width 0.48—0.58. Abnormal individuals similar to those recorded in E. fumigatus also occur in this species.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Most of the upper surface of the head yellow, becoming pale brown posteriorly, the sides and base mostly pale yellow-brown, the clypeus slightly paler. Antennae 14-segmented; segmentation variable, segment 4 usually shortest. Postclypeus length slightly less than half its width. Measurements: total length 4.25; head length (to anterior margin of clypeus) 1.28—1.30; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.90—0.94; head width 1.10—1.14; pronotum width 0.62—0.66.
